svg.aria-label: MedX — Encryption in Transit & at Rest
svg.title: MedX — Encryption in Transit & at Rest
svg.text: High-priority requirement H1 · every hop encrypted · two independent layers at rest · keys generated and held in HSM-backed KMS
no plaintext hop, inside or outside the platform
HSTS · modern AEAD ciphers only · certificate pinning in mobile apps
Service mesh · SPIFFE workload identities · certificates rotated every 24 h
Dynamic, short-lived database credentials issued by Vault
SRTP is mandatory in WebRTC · end-to-end SFrame layer when both clients support it
Certificate validation · no health data in payloads (SMS, e-mail, calendars)
Replication streams encrypted in transit and re-encrypted at rest
generated in hardware · never leave it · quorum-controlled
Disks, databases, object storage, Kafka, Redis and backups are also encrypted (AES-256, KMS keys).
At the end of the retention period, destroying a patient's DEK makes every copy unreadable — including replicas and backups.
One compromised DEK exposes one patient, not the database. Unwrapped DEKs are cached in memory ≤ 5 min to limit KMS calls.
